claim: Within the analytic crossover model of arXiv:2610.01704v1, suppose the FFT-matched adiabatic time obeys \(T(N)=\kappa(\log N)^2(1+o(1))\) for some \(\kappa>0\), and let \(N_*(p)\to\infty\) as \(p\to0\) satisfy the paper's crossover equation \[N_*(p)=\frac{1}{a\pi^2 p\,T(N_*(p))^2}+\frac{2c}{a\,{\rm d}t},\] with fixed positive \(a,c,{\rm d}t\). Then \[pN_*(p)\bigl(\log(1/p)\bigr)^4\longrightarrow\frac{1}{a\pi^2\kappa^2},\] so \(N_*(p)=\Theta(1/[p(\log(1/p))^4])\). More generally, if the noiseless adiabatic error scales as \(T^{-\gamma}\) and the crossover balance is \(N_*(p)=\Theta(1/[pT(N_*)^{1+\gamma}])\), the same \(T(N)=\Theta((\log N)^2)\) assumption gives \(N_*(p)=\Theta(1/[p(\log(1/p))^{2(1+\gamma)}])\). These are conditional consequences of the source's analytic noise model, not hardware-universal asymptotics.
integrity: Analytic proof; finite numerical replay is corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: Conditional on the source crossover equation and on T(N)=kappa(log N)^2(1+o(1)); no hardware-universal or compilation-universal asymptotic is claimed.
title: A log-fourth crossover law inside the noisy fermionic-Fourier model
